A submitted specimen (syn. material, used for billing purposes only, syn. sample) results from a specimen collection procedure and may be contained in several containers. In the pathology laboratory the submitted specimens (case), which may consist of several parts, are usually called specimens from grossing onwards.     <element id="mii-lm-patho-logical-model.Identifikation">
      <path value="mii-lm-patho-logical-model.Identifikation"/>
      <short
             value="The identifier of a pathology report (e.g. E/20/12345.1) is unique and is usually derived from the accession number (case number). It should be composed of the set ID (e.g. E/20/12345), under which all versions of a report are recorded, and the version number (e.g. 1). It is, however, also possible to use a UID (unique identifier) or GUID (global unique identifier) that is not derived from the case number. Usually the case number is used as the set ID."/>
      <definition
                  value="The identifier of a pathology report (e.g. E/20/12345.1) is unique and is usually derived from the accession number (case number). It should be composed of the set ID (e.g. E/20/12345), under which all versions of a report are recorded, and the version number (e.g. 1). It is, however, also possible to use a UID (unique identifier) or GUID (global unique identifier) that is not derived from the case number. Usually the case number is used as the set ID."/>
      <min value="1"/>
      <max value="*"/>
      <type>
        <code value="Identifier"/>
      </type>
    </element>

    <element id="mii-lm-patho-logical-model.Proben">
      <path value="mii-lm-patho-logical-model.Proben"/>
      <short value="Specimen"/>
      <definition
                  value="Physical object or collection of physical objects obtained from a patient that are regarded as a unit, are uniquely identified within the pathology facility and are the subject of one or more procedures in the workflow. A submitted specimen (syn. material, used for billing purposes only, syn. sample) results from a specimen collection procedure and may be contained in several containers. In the pathology laboratory the submitted specimens (case), which may consist of several parts, are usually called specimens from grossing onwards. Specimens may undergo one or more processing steps, usually into blocks and stained sections."/>
      <min value="1"/>
      <max value="*"/>
